2027-05-12.title: Wednesday of the Seventh Week of Easter · Sts Nereus and Achilleus; St Pancras
readings: Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock, of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers
Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth (or: Alleluia)
Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth
2027-05-12.alt: Easter weekday of the seventh week (Year I), in the days between the Ascension and Pentecost. In India the Ascension was celebrated on Sunday 9 May. Until Pentecost one of the Prefaces of the Ascension or of Easter is said, the paschal candle burns beside the ambo, and the Regina Caeli (Queen of Heaven) replaces the Angelus. Many parishes pray the novena to the Holy Spirit in these days, as the apostles prayed with Mary in the upper room. Liturgical colour: white. Optional memorials: Sts Nereus and Achilleus, martyrs, and St Pancras, martyr (colour red if one of their Masses is said). Lectionary Psalm 68:29–30, 33–35a, 35bc–36ab = NRSV 68:28–29, 32–35.
2027-05-12.verse: Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth.
theo: Paul is on his last journey to Jerusalem, and he knows what waits for him there: “imprisonment and persecutions.” He does not have time to go back to Ephesus, where he had worked for three years, so he sends for the elders of that church to meet him at the port of Miletus. Today we hear the second half of his farewell, the only speech in Acts that Paul gives to Christian leaders. It is a pastor's last will. “Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock, of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the church of God that he obtained with the blood of his own Son.” The Church is not their property; it was bought at the price of Christ's blood, and the Holy Spirit placed them in charge. Paul is honest about the danger: “savage wolves will come in among you,” and some “even from your own group will come distorting the truth.” Then he commends them “to God and to the message of his grace,” and points to his own example: “I coveted no one's silver or gold or clothing,” he worked with his own hands, and he quotes a saying of the Lord found in no Gospel: “It is more blessed to give than to receive.” The scene ends on the shore with tears. “He knelt down with them all and prayed. There was much weeping among them all; they embraced Paul and kissed him,” grieving most because they would not see his face again. The Psalm lifts the sadness into praise: “Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth.” The God who “gives power and strength to his people” will keep the flock when the shepherd has gone.

In the Gospel we hear the heart of the prayer Jesus offered at the Last Supper, a farewell even deeper than Paul's. He is going to the Father, and he prays for those he leaves behind: “Holy Father, protect them in your name that you have given me, so that they may be one, as we are one.” He does not ask for an escape: “I am not asking you to take them out of the world, but I ask you to protect them from the evil one.” Disciples are not meant to hide from the world, but neither are they meant to belong to it. And then the great petition: “Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth.” To be sanctified is to be set apart for God, made holy, and sent: “As you have sent me into the world, so I have sent them into the world.” The martyrs remembered today were sent in this way. Nereus and Achilleus were soldiers in Rome. Pope St Damasus, in an inscription he wrote for their tomb in the catacomb of Domitilla, says (in substance) that they had served a cruel order, but suddenly believed, threw down their shields and weapons, and gladly bore witness to the triumph of Christ. St Pancras was a boy of about fourteen, put to death in Rome on the Via Aurelia, probably in the persecution of Diocletian around 304. Soldiers and a teenager: the prayer of Jesus, “protect them from the evil one,” was answered in them not by sparing their lives but by keeping their faith.
outline: Ask: if you had to say goodbye to the people you love most, what would your last words be?
Point 1 · Keep watch over the flock
A Church bought with the blood of Christ and entrusted by the Spirit.
Paul's hands and the Lord's saying.
Point 3 · Sanctify them in the truth
In the world, not of it, and sent.
“Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth.”
live: Name your parish priest and your bishop in prayer today, and ask the Holy Spirit to keep them watchful and faithful.
Do one act of giving today that no one will repay: time, help, money or a kind word.
2027-05-12.prayer: Holy Father, your Son prayed for us on the night before he died: keep us in your name and make us one. Protect us from the evil one, and sanctify us in the truth, for your word is truth. Watch over the shepherds of your Church, whom the Holy Spirit has made overseers of the flock bought by the blood of Christ. By the prayers of Sts Nereus, Achilleus and Pancras, who laid down their weapons and their lives for Christ, give us courage to belong to you in the middle of the world. Come, Holy Spirit, as we wait with Mary for Pentecost. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: Paul reminds the elders that the Church was obtained “with the blood of his own Son.” At every Mass that price is placed before our eyes: the chalice of the Blood of Christ, poured out for the Church. The Eucharist is the food that keeps the flock one and holy in the truth.

quick: At Miletus Paul said farewell to the elders of Ephesus: keep watch over the flock that Christ bought with his blood.
He reminded them of the Lord's saying: it is more blessed to give than to receive; they wept and prayed together on the shore.
Jesus prayed for his disciples: protect them from the evil one, sanctify them in the truth, as you sent me, so I send them.
2027-05-12.action: Give something today, quietly, without waiting for thanks.
2027-05-12.question: Do I belong to the world, or do I live in the world as one who belongs to God?
kidsaint: Pancras was a boy of about fourteen who lived in Rome long ago. When Christians were being arrested, he did not hide his faith in Jesus. He was put to death for being a Christian, and he is a patron of children and young people. Lesson: you are never too young to be brave for Jesus.

family.explain: St Paul had to say goodbye to his friends in Ephesus, and they cried and hugged him. Before he left he reminded them of something Jesus said: it is more blessed to give than to receive. Giving makes us happier than getting! Jesus also prayed for his friends that God would protect them and make them holy.
family.intention: We pray for our parish priest and our bishop, and for all who have to say goodbye to people they love.
family.ask: Ask: “What can each of us give to someone else today?”

illus: A parish priest in a fishing village near Kollam was transferred after nine years. On his last Sunday he did not speak about himself. He handed each family a small card with the words of Acts 20:32 and said: I commend you to God and to the message of his grace. He reminded them that the parish had belonged to Christ before he came, and would belong to Christ after he left. Years later, many homes still kept that card near the family altar.

pm.open: Holy Father, keep us in your name, sanctify us in the truth, and send us into the world. Come, Holy Spirit. Amen.
share: Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock (Acts 20:28). For whom has God made me responsible, and how am I watching over them?
It is more blessed to give than to receive (Acts 20:35). When did I last experience the joy of giving?
I am not asking you to take them out of the world (John 17:15). Where do I find it hard to be a Christian in the world around me?
pm.resp: Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth.
interc: For our Pope, our bishops and our priests, that the Holy Spirit may make them watchful shepherds of the flock.
For Christians tempted to give up their faith under pressure, that they may have the courage of Nereus, Achilleus and Pancras.
For those who are saying goodbye to family, friends or their homeland, that God may comfort them.
For all who work with their hands to support their families.
For our group, that we may be one as the Father and the Son are one, and wait together for the Holy Spirit.
pm.close: Father, your Son prayed that we might be one and holy in the truth. Hear his prayer in us, and send us the Holy Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, have you ever stood at a railway station or an airport to say goodbye to someone you love? Today Paul stands on the shore at Miletus with the elders of Ephesus. He knows that he will not see them again. And his last words are not about himself, but about them and about the Church: keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock (Acts 20:28).

Paul tells them why the flock is so precious. It is the church of God that he obtained with the blood of his own Son. Every parish, every family of believers, has been bought at that price. That is why a shepherd must be watchful, and why every Christian must care for the faith of others. Paul then points to his own hands. He took nothing from them; he worked to support himself and the weak, remembering the word of the Lord Jesus: it is more blessed to give than to receive (Acts 20:35).

In the Gospel Jesus too is saying goodbye, and he prays for us. Holy Father, protect them in your name. I am not asking you to take them out of the world, but I ask you to protect them from the evil one (John 17:15). Jesus does not want us to run away from the office, the college, the market. He wants us there, but belonging to God. Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth (John 17:17).

The martyrs Nereus and Achilleus were soldiers who laid down their weapons for Christ, and Pancras was only a boy of about fourteen. They lived in the world, but they belonged to God, and the Father kept them faithful to the end. In these days before Pentecost, let us ask the Holy Spirit to make us holy in the truth, generous in giving, and faithful shepherds of whoever God has placed in our care. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul had to say goodbye to his friends, and they all cried and hugged. He told them: remember what Jesus said, it is better to give than to receive. Jesus also prayed for his friends that God would keep them safe from the evil one. Today, try to give something: share a toy, help at home, or say a kind word. Giving makes Jesus smile!

intro: Theme: “Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth.”
Two farewells: Paul on the shore at Miletus, and Jesus at the Last Supper praying for his own.

sub: Wolves and the word of grace.
q: For thus says the Lord God: I myself will search for my sheep, and will seek them out.
Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock, of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the church of God that he obtained with the blood of his own Son.
points.apply: This week, pray each day for your parish priest and your bishop by name, and do one thing to help the faith of someone in your care.

sub: A saying of the Lord kept by Paul.
q: A generous person will be enriched, and one who gives water will get water.
In all this I have given you an example that by such work we must support the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus, for he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’
points.apply: Choose one person who cannot repay you, and give them your time or help before Sunday.

sub: Not taken out of the world.
Holy and sent, like the martyrs.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth.
points.apply: Until Pentecost, read a few verses of the Gospel each morning before you go out into the world, and ask: Lord, make me holy in your truth today.

concl: Paul's farewell and the prayer of Jesus tell us the same thing: the Church belongs to God, bought by the blood of Christ and kept by the Father's name.
We are left in the world, not to be swallowed by it, but to be holy in the truth and sent, as the martyrs were.
2027-05-12.resolve: Pray each day until Pentecost: Holy Father, keep me in your name; Come, Holy Spirit.
